Cycling in Puglia

Italy's sun-soaked heel

RIDE WHERE THE PROS TRAIN

Puglia offers a different side of Italy: quiet roads, endless olive groves, whitewashed villages and spectacular Mediterranean coastline, all with remarkably little traffic. It is the perfect destination for cyclists looking to enjoy long, flowing miles while discovering a region still largely untouched by mass cycling tourism.

Our tours explore the best of Puglia, from the rolling roads of the Valle d’Itria to the dramatic coastline and remote countryside of the Salento peninsula. Ride through ancient landscapes, discover charming villages and enjoy some of Italy’s finest regional cuisine along the way.

Our aim is simple: to create an unforgettable cycling holiday with exceptional routes, authentic experiences and the very best of Puglia. Our tours explore the region’s finest roads, from the iconic climb of Rocacorba to peaceful farm roads winding through forests, villages and vineyards. Ride the same roads as the world’s best cyclists, enjoy exceptional Catalan food and discover why so many riders choose Girona as their home away from home.

Our aim is simple: to create an unforgettable cycling holiday with exceptional routes, authentic experiences and the very best of Girona.

Puglia's cycling appeal comes from its rhythm — gently rolling terrain rather than sharp mountains, which makes it one of the best regions in Italy for building genuine volume and base fitness. Roads wind past centuries-old olive groves, dry-stone walls and the region's famous trulli, the conical stone houses unique to the Valle d'Itria.

Puglia forms the heel of Italy's boot, stretching along both the Adriatic and Ionian coasts in the country's far southeast. Whitewashed towns like Ostuni and Alberobello sit among some of the oldest olive groves in the world, while the Salento peninsula further south offers dramatic coastal roads with some of Italy's clearest water. Given its flatter, more rolling terrain and near-constant sunshine, Puglia is a destination where visitors can enjoy a holiday full of relaxed but genuine riding, cultural discovery and the thrill of exploring a part of Italy most cyclists have never considered.

When you think of Puglian food, expect one of Italy's most distinctive regional cuisines. Orecchiette pasta, exceptional burrata, and some of the country's best olive oil are all Puglian staples, alongside the bold red wines of Primitivo and Negroamaro grown across the region. There are countless masserie and trattorias throughout Puglia, set in wonderful countryside and coastal locations, and we will bring you to the best

PUGLIA FACTS

LOCATION

Puglia forms the heel of Italy's boot in the country's far southeast, with coastline along both the Adriatic and Ionian Seas. Its landscape is largely flat to gently rolling, dominated by olive groves and farmland rather than mountains.

CLIMATE

Puglia enjoys one of the sunniest, driest climates in Italy, with hot summers reaching 30-33°C along the coast and mild winters — making it a popular year-round and off-season riding destination for cyclists seeking dependable weather.

CUISINE

Puglian cuisine is one of Italy's most distinctive regional traditions, built around orecchiette pasta, exceptional burrata and some of the world's best olive oil. The Primitivo and Negroamaro wines of the region pair perfectly with a day spent in the saddle.

TERRAIN

Puglia's largely flat and gently rolling terrain makes it ideal for building genuine training volume in comfort. Roads wind through ancient olive groves and whitewashed towns like Ostuni and Alberobello, with dramatic coastal riding along the Salento peninsula further south.
